direction.name: The contact sheet
direction.idea: Show everything at once, small, in order. The work is laid out like a photographer's contact sheet or an archive drawer: dozens of small frames in strict rows, with all text set at one small size. Nothing is featured, which is the point: the volume and consistency of the body of work is the statement, and the visitor does the choosing. It suits people and studios whose strength is range and output.
direction.composition: The name, or one sentence about the work, sits at display size (6–9vw) across the top of the first screen, and the sheet begins directly under it, still inside the first screen. The first screen opens with three or four short blocks of small text across the top on a 12-column grid (who, what, where to reach them), all at 14–16px, and immediately below, the sheet begins: rows of thumbnails at a fixed height (90–140px) with their natural widths, 6–10px gaps, each project forming a run of four to eight frames preceded by its title in the same small text. The sheet fills the whole page width edge to edge with 16–20px margins. Hovering a run dims the others and shows that project's one-line description in a fixed position. A single enlarged frame may interrupt the sheet once per screen at four times the size.
direction.typography: One face. The name at display size on the first screen; everything else at one text size and one small size; hierarchy below the name comes from position and from a single brighter ink for titles.
direction.colour: Black or white ground, so the thumbnails are the only colour.
direction.imagery: Many images: at least 24 frames to make a sheet. They can be project photographs from the dealt set cropped to mixed ratios, or page captures of the work. Square corners, no captions on the frames.
direction.richness: Density and order. The mass of small images forms a texture; the strict rows keep it calm.
direction.pitfalls: With fewer than about 20 images it looks unfinished; choose another direction. Do not add a big headline above the sheet. On a phone the frames become two per row at a fixed height and each run scrolls sideways. Rows that run past the right edge read as clipped in screenshots and to most visitors: wrap the frames onto the next line, or end each row inside the grid.

hero.name: Text band, then sheet
hero.blueprint: A black or white field on a seven-column grid with 14px margins and 14px gaps. There is no display type: everything is set at one size, 16px, in one weight. The top band is plain text hanging from a line 20px below the top edge: the name in column one; one sentence on availability in column two; a list of five or six services from column three; a longer list of clients or awards from column five; and two links, profile and the single contact action, at the right end of column seven. Lists run one item per line. Below the lists about 300px of ground is left empty. At mid-height the sheet begins: one thumbnail per column, each the full column width (about 190px) at its natural ratio, top-aligned, with the project title in the text size above the first frame of each run of two to four frames. Rows continue below the fold with 40px between them. Frames have square corners and sit directly on the ground with no border and no caption on the image.
hero.mobile: The grid becomes two columns with 12px gaps. The name and the availability sentence take the top; services and clients sit side by side under them as two short lists at 15px. An 80px gap follows, then the sheet: two frames per row at natural ratios, each project title above its first frame. The contact action is a text link fixed bottom-right.
hero.headline: None at display size: the name is set at 16px with the rest of the text, and one sentence of up to 60 characters says what the person does.

type.note: An American gothic for headings over a sober transitional serif for reading, the pairing of a newspaper front page. Suits essays, annual reports, archives and finance pages that have real paragraphs.

palette.name: Navy on white
palette.note: Pure white pages with navy type sit between full-bleed photographs, opening on near-black and closing on a warm grey footer. Tangerine is one small tab or button, never larger than a thumbnail.

motion.name: Index with preview
motion.description: Rows of text are the navigation through the work; pointing at a row brings up its image in one fixed frame and dims the other rows. On touch screens each row shows its image inline instead. Fast and exact (about 240ms crossfade), no lag behind the pointer. Recipe: 'Index with preview, anchored to the row' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Small frames, wide space
sections.blueprint: A flat, quiet viewport 100svh tall in which about 70% of the screen is empty. At mid-height a single row of small portrait frames runs across and off both sides: each frame 11vw wide and 24svh tall (roughly 2:3), spaced 5vw apart, vertically centred, six or seven visible at 1440. Frames have square corners and sit directly on the ground with no border. The row scrolls sideways by drag or trackpad (`overflow-x: auto` with the scrollbar hidden) and may hold 12–24 frames. One line of text overlaps the top-left of the first frame by 12px: a title of two or three words at 20–24px followed by the count, placed above the frame in the stacking order. Hovering a frame scales it to 1.1 from its centre over 250ms; nothing else moves. No captions under frames, no arrows, and no other text in the section.
sections.mobile: The row sits at 45% of an 80svh section. Frames are 34vw wide at 2:3 and 5vw apart, so two and a half are visible and the row scrolls by touch with snapping. The title line sits 20px above the row at the left margin.

sections.name: Narrow column, empty field
sections.blueprint: A single text column 300–340px wide, its left edge at 15% of the viewport width, starting 64px below the section top. It holds four or five short paragraphs at 15–16px with leading 1.5 and one blank line between them; the first paragraph is in medium weight and full ink, the rest in regular weight and the soft ink. No heading, no image, no button; one underlined text link may end the last paragraph. The remaining three-quarters of the 1440 screen is untouched ground, and the section is only as tall as the text plus 160px of padding below. The column's left edge must match a line used elsewhere on the page (the wordmark's left edge or a later column). Where the page has a large object or a fixed photograph, this column is the small text beside it. Holds 90–150 words comfortably.
sections.mobile: The column becomes 78% of the width, left-aligned at the 20px margin, so a strip of empty ground remains on the right as a deliberate margin. Text stays at 15–16px with the first paragraph in medium weight. Padding is 72px above and 96px below.

sections.name: Quiet ledger, side preview
sections.blueprint: A plain ledger in one column 560px wide whose left edge sits at 22% of the viewport width. A heading of two or three words at 24–28px in medium weight, then 32px of space, then one row per project, 44px tall: the name at 16px in full ink at the left, the kind of work at 14px in the soft ink starting at 55% of the column, and the year right-aligned with tabular figures. Nothing is drawn between rows; the three fixed starts make the columns. Hovering or focusing a row keeps it in full ink, drops the others to the soft ink, and shows that project's image in the empty area right of the column: a 4:3 frame 300px wide, `position: absolute`, its top aligned to the hovered row, 64px from the column's right edge, appearing with a 150ms fade. Holds 6–20 rows; group by year with 28px of extra space.
sections.mobile: The column fills the width with 20px margins. Rows are 52px tall: name at the left, year at the right, kind of work on a second line at 13px. There is no hover preview; instead the first three projects each show a 16:10 image at full column width above their row.

sections.name: Three photographs, then a field
sections.blueprint: Two parts with no gap between them. First, a strip of three photographs butted edge to edge across the full viewport, each one third wide and 40svh tall, `object-fit: cover`, no gutters and no captions; give all three the same treatment. Directly beneath, a band in one flat palette colour, about 44svh tall. In the band, columns 1–7: the closing statement at 26–30px over three lines in the band's assigned ink, with exactly one phrase underlined by a 4px bar (`text-decoration-thickness: 4px; text-underline-offset: 6px`), and that phrase is the link; two lines at 16px follow 32px lower. In the lower-right corner, columns 11–12, a small portrait photograph (4:5, about 150px wide) sits 40px from the band's edges: the person who will answer. There is no button; the underlined phrase is the action.
sections.mobile: The strip becomes one full-width photograph at 4:3 with the other two side by side beneath it at half width each, still gutterless. The band follows: statement at 22px, the two small lines, and the portrait at 96px wide in the bottom-right corner.

sections.name: A footer of tiles
sections.blueprint: The footer is the last two rows of a board: filled tiles with 8px gaps and 8–12px outer margins, every cell used. Upper row, each tile 220px tall: a statement tile in columns 1–4 with one sentence at 24px top-left and the legal text at 12px bottom-left; a navigation tile in columns 5–7 with a plain list at 16px; a tile in columns 8–9 giving the city and local time as text; an email tile in columns 10–12 with the address at 20px as a link, bottom-left. Lower row, 320px tall: a tile in the ink colour spanning columns 1–8 with the wordmark set large (about 9vw) and centred, and a tile in the accent colour in columns 9–12 with a two-to-four-word invitation top-left at 28px and an arrow, drawn as inline SVG with 4px strokes, in its bottom-right corner; the whole accent tile is a link.
sections.mobile: Two columns of tiles with 6px gaps: the wordmark tile full width first at 160px tall, the accent tile full width next, then navigation and email side by side, then time and statement. Every tile keeps 20px padding and top-left text.

references.name: Gil Huybrecht
references.idea: A portfolio as a contact sheet: every project is a numbered run of miniature page screenshots on black, and all text is set at one small size.
references.hero: Black field on a seven-column grid with 14px margins. The top band is plain white text at one size, about 16px: name in column one, availability in column two, a services list from column three, a longer awards list from column five, then 'Profile' and 'Email me' at the right. List items are indented one step under their label. Below the lists roughly 300px of black is left empty. At mid-height the thumbnail grid begins: one small website screenshot per column, about 190px wide, each topped by a number at its right corner, with the project name over the first of each run. Two tiny toggle chips sit in the bottom corners.
references.type: One neo-grotesk at a single size, about 16px (1.1vw), medium-bold with tight tracking, white on black, for everything: name, lists, labels, numbers, footer. There is no headline; hierarchy comes only from column position and indentation.
references.colour: #000000 #fcfcfc #272727 #8a8a8a — Pure black with white text; the only colour is whatever appears inside the screenshot thumbnails. Inactive toggle words drop to mid-grey on a dark grey chip.
references.imagery: Miniature full-page captures of the designer's client sites, uncropped at natural aspect ratios, square corners, no frames or shadows, about 190px wide, sitting directly on black.
references.layout: Seven equal columns with 14px gutters and margins for the whole page. Thumbnails align to columns but not to rows: each hangs from its own label at its own height, so bottoms are ragged. Projects flow continuously and wrap across rows.

sections.description: A seven-column field of screenshot thumbnails on black. Each project is a consecutive run of four to six thumbnails; the project name sits above the first, and every thumbnail carries its sequence number right-aligned above it in the same 16px white. Thumbnails keep their real proportions, so a row mixes 100px-tall and 280px-tall items with ragged bottoms and about 90px of black between rows. Runs break mid-row and continue on the next line with no divider.

View toggles. Two fixed chip pairs sit in the viewport's bottom corners: the left switches between a grid and a gallery view, the right between a normal and a novelty perspective mode. Each pair is a small dark-grey rounded rectangle containing two words, the active one white and the inactive grey, at the same 16px as all other text.

After about a screen of empty black, one band of text on the same seven columns: year and privacy link stacked at the left, then two columns of stacked social links, then two single links toward the right edge. Same size and weight as the header, no rule, no logo.

steal: Set every piece of text on the page at one size and weight and build hierarchy only from column position and a one-step indent under labels.
Show projects as numbered runs of uncropped page screenshots at natural heights on a strict column grid, leaving the bottoms ragged.
Leave a deliberate 300px void between the text header and the first row of work so the lists read as a letterhead.
references.media: A contact-sheet wall: one fixed WebGL canvas draws about 84 full-page screenshots of client sites at a single 190px width and their native ratios, every page of each project in reading order. Once scrolled, every screen is about three rows, roughly 48% picture and 52% black, with text under 1% and the labels above each frame, never on it; there is no video.
references.motion: The preloader counts at about 13% a second for some 7-8s while the screenshot textures load, although the document loaded in 1.66s; then the first-row thumbnails rise into their slots in random order and a dark veil lifts. Lenis over a 4440px scroll proxy redraws the fixed wall with no pins or reveals; panel and hover moves use transform .75s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1), and pictures fade over 1s ease-out on the phone.

references.name: Oimachi
references.idea: A studio homepage that behaves like a dense dashboard: work, posts, experiments and testimonials tiled edge to edge with 8px gutters instead of spaced-out sections.
references.archetype: other: left statement over media row with posts sidebar
references.hero: Charcoal ground (#181818) with only 8px side margins. Top-left: a round logo, then five tiny black rectangular chips with bold white 13px labels; top-right a contact chip and a theme toggle. The headline starts at the left margin about 160px down: two lines of light grotesk at 52px (3.6vw), tight tracking, with one word in italic serif. From 280px to the bottom edge runs a three-part row: two tall images butted together (each about 535x610px: a hand holding a phone on black, a man in a printed tee) and a 330px sidebar of blog posts, each a bold 14px title, two grey truncated lines and a small-radius thumbnail.
references.type: Aeonik throughout: light 52px for the headline, regular 20 to 24px for mid-page statements, bold 13px for nav chips and post titles, 12px grey captions. Single words switch to an italic serif inside headings. The scale is deliberately small; nothing exceeds 3.6vw.
references.colour: #181818 #070707 #2a2a2a #ffffff #ff4a2b #8a8a8a — Charcoal ground with black chips and white text, unchanged from section to section; colour arrives only through work thumbnails in orange-red, purple and green. A light-mode toggle exists.
references.imagery: Client work as photographs, UI shots, brand graphics and generated explorations; rectangles with 4px corners in tight 4:3 strips and a masonry of mixed aspect ratios, each with a tiny caption.
references.layout: 8px margins and 4 to 8px gutters everywhere. Short three-line statements at about 22px are indented to the 33% or 66% column and act as section breaks between tightly tiled image grids. Text columns stay narrow; images take two-thirds of the width.

sections.description: Rows divided by hairlines, each about 120px tall. The left third holds a small client icon, the name in 12px bold and the sector in grey at the top, with a two-line 11px description pinned to the bottom of the row. The right two-thirds holds three equal 4:3 thumbnails with 4px gaps. Above the list a three-line statement at 22px sits at the 66% column with a text link far right.

A statement at the 66% column introduces a dense masonry of experiments: around twenty tiles in six uneven columns with 4px gaps, sizes from 90px squares to a 280x160px feature tile, mixing screenshots, posters, renders and textures. Every tile has a 10px caption beneath in the form 'Name / Type'. No hover chrome is visible; it reads like a contact sheet.

Two wide video stills side by side, each cropped to a shallow band about 95px tall, showing a person mid-interview. Under each: a black square play chip, a small company icon, then the name in bold 12px and the role in grey. There is no quotation text at all; the testimonial is the video.

Four equal columns headed at 20px, each a list of 11px grey links prefixed by a tiny coloured square icon. Below, a large white circle logo with a black rounded square inside at far left, a two-line 20px question at the 33% column, and a small white booking chip with email and phone set inline beside it.

steal: Shrink page margins and gutters to 8px and tile media edge to edge so a portfolio reads as a working dashboard rather than a brochure.
Put a live blog or news sidebar inside the hero next to the showreel, so the first screen proves the studio is active.
Style nav links as tiny solid rectangular chips sitting directly in the page corner instead of in a bar.
references.media: A muted, looping reel of brand work covers about 51% of the first screen (75% of the width, 68% of the height) in a black well beside a rail of three 16:9 news thumbnails. Below: third-split rows with a label column on the left and three 3:2 tiles on the right two thirds, half-and-half video testimonials, an 8-column masonry of mixed ratios with small captions, and a text panel beside a photo stack; 34 images and 17 videos, client work supplying all the colour on near-black.
references.motion: There is no preloader and only the reel cuts after 400ms; a single ScrollTrigger scrubs the news rail at 0.8 so it drifts as the hero leaves, with no smooth-scroll library and no pins. Cards grow an outline over 0.5s on an ease-out-quint, images move over 0.6-0.8s on cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1), links fade colour over 0.2s, and 33 skeleton shimmers (1.2s) hold space while media loads, with no reduced-motion rule.

references.name: Miu Miu A House That We Shaped
references.idea: A bag campaign set inside one furnished room, a period salon with hand-painted vermilion and emerald doors rendered in real time: you find the products by touching objects in the room rather than by scrolling, so the house is the interface and the brand mood comes from the paint on the set.
references.hero: An entry gate on a flat deep navy field: a centred white block about 500px wide, a 26px bold uppercase kicker and three 58px (≈4vw) bold uppercase title lines at a 108px pitch, each force-justified so the words hug both edges and the last word is letter-spaced across the full measure; then a two-line 14px deck, a small sound notice at the top and a light Enter button about 100x48 at the bottom centre, a spinner until 1.2s. After Enter the room fills the screen: the camera opens tight on a hand-painted vermilion door and pulls back over a few seconds to the wide set while yellow subtitle lines cross-fade; then one pulsing hotspot on a notebook and a 273x100 paper-beige card at the bottom centre name the first task. No header, logo or menu.
references.type: Work Sans alone at 400 and 700. The gate title in bold uppercase at about 58px, force-justified; after entry the largest text is 16px (1.1vw) regular, leading 1.2, black on paper beige in the task card, and subtitles are about 14px in yellow. Type is fluid from a root unit of about 10px at 1440. The gate title runs to four lines; under the house rules it is two.
references.colour: #0c0f60 #ffffff #948c89 #7c6958 #776453 #fcf5e6 #ffe100 — Gate: navy at 100% with white type. Room: a greige wall (about 45%), a taupe dado (31%) and a mushroom carpet (24%), with two painted doors, vermilion (about 8%) and emerald (about 5%), carrying all the brand colour and a mustard lamp shade as a small accent. The interface is one warm paper beige with black text.
references.imagery: A photoreal but soft real-time set with a matte, slightly underexposed, low-contrast filmic grade: doors in rough hand-brushed paint with the frame showing through the strokes, and a red paint stroke along the dado rail like unfinished work. The canvas has no corners or frame. Product pictures arrive later as a scattered collage of rotated portrait figures (from the stylesheet, not captured).
references.layout: No document flow: exactly one 1440x900 viewport, scrollY 0 on all twelve wheel steps. The gate centres a 500px block with about 470px of navy either side. In the room the wall runs to y≈406, the dado to y≈686 and the carpet below; the hero door stands just left of centre and the second door is cut by the right edge. The interface is four docked pieces on under 3% of the frame.

sections.description: The intro film: the camera starts tight on the vermilion door, a lamp vignette at the left and an armchair at the right, and pulls back over a few seconds to the wide room while three short manifesto lines cross-fade as a 14px yellow subtitle about 52px above the bottom.

The resting room as the interface: the vermilion door (about 266x600) at x≈590-856, a lamp and a table of stacked notebooks on the left, the armchair on the right, the emerald door in perspective on the side wall. One pulsing white hotspot about 36px with a 70px ring sits on the notebook, the task card names it, and a 44px sound toggle sits 20px from the bottom-right corner.

The end page, known from the stylesheet only: five portrait figures of about 3:4 scattered with rotations from -47 to 9 degrees like photographs thrown on a table, with a fluid end title and lines that underline one after another.

steal: Put the colour in the set, not the interface: keep about 90% of the frame in muted greige, taupe and mushroom, let two saturated accents on objects carry the brand mood, and keep the interface to one warm paper tone with black text.

Open with a camera pull-back from tight on the hero object to the wide resting composition over a few seconds, and fade the first task in only when the camera settles (opacity 0.5s cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1)); place the hero object just off centre and crop a second one by the frame edge so the room continues past the screen.

When the page is a scene, limit the interface to a few docked pieces covering under 3% of the frame: one subtitle line, one task card, one hotspot on the object to touch, one sound toggle. Under the house rules the first screen still names the product and offers a plain route to the collection.
references.media: The gate is pure type on navy; after entry one fixed WebGL canvas renders the whole room at 100% of the viewport from the first frame, with no img or video elements in the captured state and the interface on under 3% of the frame. The intro is a camera move inside the scene, not a video.
references.motion: Twelve wheel steps leave the room unchanged apart from a sway of up to about 18px, while the camera pull-back plays on its own clock and then the hotspot ring pulses from scale 1 to 2.2 over 2s cubic-bezier(.215,.61,.355,1) as the task card fades in over 0.55-0.65s. Most moves use easeOutQuint (.23,1,.32,1, 37 uses) or expo-out (.16,1,.3,1) for 1.6s mask wipes, and the pulse, wiggle and jitter loops run with no reduced-motion rule after a 4.2s load.
